source.citation: Oyola SO, Ariani CV, Hamilton WL, et al. (2016) Whole genome sequencing of Plasmodium falciparum from dried blood spots using selective whole genome amplification. Malaria Journal 15:597.
source.tables: Table S1 (Additional file 1, slide 5 of 12936_2016_1641_MOESM1_ESM.pptx) gives the Probe_10 sequences. Sequences for primers 11-28 were never published, so Probe_20 and Probe_28 cannot be reconstructed.
source.designed_with: a published PERL script selecting up to 100 8-12mers with predicted Tm <= 30 C, ranked by desired/contaminating (P. falciparum vs human) k-mer frequency ratio
source.reaction: 30 units phi29, stepdown from 35 C to 30 C over 16 h then 65 C for 15 min, 2.5 uM each primer, >=5 ng input, 50 uL
source.modification: one 3' phosphorothioate bond per primer (written '*' in the source table, stripped here)
source.notes: Three NESTED pools were compared on mock samples - Probe_10 (first 10 primers), Probe_20 (first 20), Probe_28 (all 28). Probe_10 was chosen for all subsequent work on yield and cost, so the smallest of three nested pools won. This independently replicates the nested-set result in Leichty and Brisson (2014), where the 2-primer SR2 beat the 10-primer SR1 it was drawn from. Only Probe_10's sequences were published, so the comparison is recorded but the losing pools cannot be scored. Outcome: >18-fold enrichment of parasite DNA; 73.2% (sd 4.4, N=5) of reads mapped to P. falciparum against <1% for standard WGA. Applied to 156 malaria patients including 120 paired dried-blood-spot / venous-blood samples, >99% SNP concordance. Parasitaemia threshold for >=5x coverage over 50% of the genome was 0.03%.

outcome.note: smallest of three nested pools; chosen on yield and cost
